sentences.text: This appeal has been preferred as against the order of acquittal passed in C.C.No.1441 of 2019 dated 11.06.2024 on the file of learned Metropolitan Magistrate cum Fast Track Court No.II, Egmore at Allikulam, Chennai for the offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

The appellant is the complainant and filed a complaint as against the respondent for offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, alleging that the respondent issued three cheques in order to repay the loan amount on 09.10.2018.
All the three cheques were presented for collection and the same were returned for the reason 'funds insufficient'.
After causing statutory notice, the appellant filed a complaint and the same has been taken cognizance by the trial court in C.C.No.4441 of 2019.

On the side of the appellant / complainant, P.W.1, viz.,
K.Kishorekumar Reddy, Power of Attorney of the appellant was examined on behalf of the appellant and marked exhibits Ex.P.1 to P.18.

On the side of the respondent, he was examined as D.W.1 and no D.V.Sivakumar Reddy vs T.Ranganathan on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57269887/
1 documents were marked.

On perusal of the materials placed on record, the trial court found that the respondent is not guilty of the offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act and dismissed the complaint lodged by the appellant herein.
Aggrieved by the same, the present appeal has been preferred.
3. The learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the appellant had entered into an agreement with one Mohan kumar for purchase of the property owned by him.
The appellant also advanced a sum of Rs.84 Lakhs in favour of Mohan kumar.
The respondent acted as a mediator between them and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 21/07/2025 02:49:45 pm ) he assured that the sale deed will be executed in favour of the appellant.

Subsequently, the said Mohankumar failed to execute the deed, as such, the respondent and said Mohankumar entered into Memorandum of Understanding, in which the respondent undertook to settle the amount, which was paid to the said Mohankumar by the appellant herein.
In pursuant to the said Memorandum of Understanding, the respondent also issued letters through email and issued cheques.
Therefore, he categorically admitted his liability and issued cheques.
Further, all the cheques issued by the respondent were dishonoured to the appellant, the respondent did not deny the signature and issuance of cheques.
Therefore, the appellant had discharged his initial burden as contemplated under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, even then, the trial court acquitted the respondent.
The learned counsel further relied upon the Memorandum of Understanding and the email letters issued by the respondent, which are marked as Exhibits.

4. Per contra, the specific case of the respondent was that the appellant and the respondent lodged a complaint even in the year 2018 as against the said Mohankumar and now the said Mohankumar is facing prosecution.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and perused the documents placed on record.
Though notice through court was sent to the respondent and the private notice was served on the respondent, there is no representation for the respondent.
6. Admittedly, the land was owned by the said Mohan kumar and he received a sum of Rs.84 Lakhs from the appellant as an advance to register sale deed in favour of the appellant herein.
The respondent acted as a mediator between them and he did not receive any amount.

7.A perusal of the Memorandum of Understanding, which was entered between the respondent and Mohankumar revealed that the respondent had undertaken to pay a sum of Rs.84 Lakhs in favour of the appellant.

In pursuant to the settlement, the appellant herein will withdraw the complaint registered in Crime No.357 of 2018, therefore, admittedly, the respondent did not receive any single penny from the appellant herein, as per the undertaking entered between the respondent and the said Mohankumar.
Hence the respondent also issued letters and emails and on receipt of the statutory notice, the respondent issued reply notice dated 05.02.2019, which was marked as Ex.P.17.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
8. On perusal of the reply notice, it is seen that the respondent had taken a specific stand that the cheques, which were issued for security purpose was presented for collection.

The appellant lodged D.V.Sivakumar Reddy vs T.Ranganathan on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57269887/
2 complaint before CCB, Chennai and the same has been registered in Crime No.357 of 2018 for offence under Section 420 of IPC.

sentences.text: The said Mohankumar has filed a quash petition before this Court to quash the FIR and he had taken a specific stand that he did not borrow or receive any amount from the appellant herein, the respondent stood as a guarantor.
Further, the respondent had taken a specific stand that the claim itself is a legally barred debt, since the cheques were issued for security purpose.
The alleged amount was transferred in favour of the said Mohankumar long back.

Further,
there is no legally enforceable debt.

The respondent also proceeded with the complaint as against the appellant for debt and forgery, accordingly, the respondent also lodged a complaint as against the appellant and it is under investigation.
9.

That apart, one Kishorekumar, who is the Power of Attorney of the appellant was examined as P.W.1 on behalf of the appellant and he categorically deposed that on 09.07.2014, the said amount was paid to the said Mohankumar and for the said amount, the respondent undertakes to repay and i s s u e d c h e q u e s i n N o v e m b e r , 2 0 1 8 , t h e r e f o r e , t h e d e b t i t s e l f i s b a r r e d b y https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 21/07/2025 02:49:45 pm ) limitation.
Further, the appellant admitted that the respondent acted as associate to Mohankumar and he did not receive any amount.

Even after receipt of reply notice, the appellant failed to prove that the cheques were issued for legally enforceable debt, therefore, the respondent categorically rebutted presumption under Sections 118 and 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Hence the trial court rightly acquitted the respondent and this Court finds no reason to interfere with the decision of the trial court.
In view of the above, the present appeal is dismissed.
